title: Рубли вместо долларов и пропажа Пашки  (Rubles Instead of Dollars and Pashka's Disappearance)

segments.t: When the debt collector returns, Lyova proudly hands over the hundred thousand rubles gathered by the cooks, only for the thug to laugh and clarify that Chef Barinov owes a hundred thousand dollars. Meanwhile, Nastya brings Pashka the turtle back to work, where it promptly wanders into the kitchen.
Короче, чтобы деньги к вечеру были.
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
'Hey head chef, did you shred the cabbage?' In Russian, the idea of 'head chef' flows naturally into 'to shred' without extra filler words. Nastya answers right away.
'Did you shred the cabbage, I asked?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'cabbage' before landing on 'to shred'.
'Is this supposed to be some kind of joke?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'this' before landing on 'such'.
'What is this?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'this' and finishing on 'what'. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'A little misunderstanding.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'not' and 'little hitch' in a few short words.
'Just like that.' The meaning hinges on 'there you go' working together with 'like this' in spoken Russian.
Короче, чтобы деньги к вечеру были.
'Long story short, have the money ready by tonight.' The plural past ending '-li' on the verb for 'be' covers a group or the polite 'you'. Nastya answers right away.
'Nastya, come over here.' Nastya anchors the line on 'Nastya', while 'here' completes the thought.
'What is this thing?' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'this' and 'what' in a few short words.
'That is Pashka.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'this' before landing on 'Pasha'. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'What is this? That is Pashka?' In Russian, the idea of 'this' flows naturally into 'Pasha' without extra filler words.
'What, did you not recognize him?' Nastya raises the pitch on 'recognised' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Alright, let's hear the whole conversation once more from start to finish.
Короче, чтобы деньги к вечеру были.

When you watch Scene 14 of Episode 10, listen out for the exchange around rubles instead of dollars and pashka's disappearance — you will recognize every Russian phrase right away. See you in the next scene.
